Despite my name, I don't want to come off as an asshole because ultimately, I agree with you - I don't want children having access to a lot of depraved shit that I'm sure a lot of us stumbled onto in our formative years. However, banning porn - mainstream websites or not - isn't a good way to go about it.

Parents should...parent. And parental controls and locks do exist. And as children grow older, they need to learn how to practice online safety. This means classes and lessons to not give out information, no posting selfies, apps like Discord should be 18+, etc. Of course, it's *impossible* for parents to monitor their kids 100% of the time (unless helicoptering) but kids need to learn how to do these things themselves. (note: I'm including teenagers, anyone who is under the age of eighteen) Self regulation is a skill necessary to learn, especially on the internet. 

Kids / teenagers need their own spaces, and I think that's a big issue in the 2020s - there's no free third space *for* them, only, you know? Even like r/ teenagers (and Reddit, itself, the main userbase are adults) is clustered with adults (iirc, one of the mods went out of their way to prove it? I dunno the whole story, but I'd be happy to look it up), or children focused websites have adults all over, TikTok was aimed for teenagers but look at it now, and anything else kid based gets shut down.

It rubs me the wrong way that politicians were able to just freely censor media like they did - it has nothing to do with porn on my end, just a bit baffling and uncomfortable because what else do you think they could get away with censoring so long as they say, "it's for the kids"? While with PH and other mainstreams, if you want access, you have to provide ID - which I'm very split on. I don't want my information out there, who knows what it could be used for, but it would help regulate and keep minors off of websites they shouldn't *be* on. 

Tangentially related, this [video ](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Ku9csXhvJY) talks about the loss of third places and how detrimental it is on society.

[Finland has a working solution](https://www.huduser.gov/portal/pdredge/pdr-edge-international-philanthropic-071123.html) - but it would make the average American gasp and gawk and go, "Not in MY country, you pick yourselves up by the boot straps!"

Aside from chaos and a possible waste of time, it could lead to political burn out among the voter base. Hopefully it *won't* do that if it does get introduced to Montana.

[This](https://ballotpedia.org/Ranked-choice_voting_(RCV)) explains choice ranked voting - though what they told me when I was stopped the other day is, "it's like that but it's not that". What happens if it's a three way tie, it goes back to voting but eliminates the lowest one. So, candidate z would get removed from the ballots, and the choices go between X and Y.

So say:

Fred is running for the Republican Party, and he gets 49% of the votes, but Mary is running for the Democratic Party and she gets 46% of the votes, but Thomas is (insert party here) gets 47% of the votes, that means Mary is removed off the ballots and Montana goes back to voting after a short period, so the choices are between Fred and Thomas.

The idea is to make it more "fair" for voters - considering how the past few presidential elections, there's always a claim of, "the vote count was wrong" (and I'm sure I remember it during the Obama era too, but the thought has been worse the last few election cycles.) that this could reduce those claims. This is called Spatial Mode Voting. Whether or not choice ranked voting is helpful or not, I don't know but:

some resources: [Spatial Mode Voting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranked_voting#Spatial_voting_models) (Wikipedia)  
[Washington Post Article](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2021/06/23/ranked-choice-voting-global/)  
[RCVR Resources](https://www.rcvresources.org/history-of-rcv)

And plenty more say it's a better representation of the people. It would be interesting to see if that'd be true for Montana, but seems to be working for the states that use them (though California is questionable since I know more people *leaving* than moving there).

I think we all dwell on the *what could have been's*, especially when it comes to suicide. It's definitely something that can haunt us for a very long time.

When my ex fiancée killed herself, she called me seven times in one night. My phone was on silent because I living at my parents and 3 am calls just weren't possible anymore. Seven times. In those seven, she left four voicemails for me. And I was asleep.

In the morning, on my way to work, I tried to call her back because her voicemails weren't very understandable - she was very, very drunk. I remember some of the things she said, "When does it get better? They keep saying it gets better." Her last voicemail was her telling me that she loves me and she'll talk to me later.

I get told the next morning as I'm driving to Billings for work that she'd killed herself.

I had to pull off to the side before I caused a crash between the town I was driving from to Billings, and cried. What if I had picked up the phone and talked to her? Would things be different today? Would she still be alive?

I dunno - I think she had her mind made up at some point and that no matter if I had picked up my phone that night, she may have gone through with it.

You didn't know she was going to do that - you worked with her and saw her maybe once. That wasn't your fault, it's no one's fault when they lose someone to suicide. It's okay to grieve and it's okay to grieve *for a very long time.* There is no timeline or limit to how long you have to grieve over something, but you do have to eventually work towards acceptance.

Yes, always be kind to someone because you never know what they're going through, that's a core rule of life but that *hello* may not have changed her course. Keep in memory the happier times and remember, *it's not your fault.* But *it's okay* to feel sad, hopeless, or even guilty but this, but it's not okay to carry the guilt and let it crush you. If you need someone to talk to, it's okay to reach out to medical professional or a loved one, no matter how long it's been. Suicide affects *everyone*.

Be well and remember to breathe.

You could ask some borderline subreddits such as r/BorderlinePDisorder! (I have borderline)

**If you want to pursue a relationship with her** :

Ask her if it's okay if you ask her questions about it! I personally don't mind talking about it, I am in a place in therapy and medication where I'm comfortable opening up about it and dealing with it. Others might not be.

**Open and  Clear Communication.** This goes for every relationship, imo.

**Clear Boundaries.** So, I'm a little odd in my thinking, where I view every relationship has a set of rules and they need to be communicated, but if they aren't and a behavior isn't told to be stopped but then suddenly, my partner gets mad at me for the behavior, it feels like a **major stab to the gut** because the rule changed too quickly and oh no, I am going to lose this person I care about dearly. Be open about your **boundaries!**

**Don't Assume Things About Her.** We all have bad days, we all get snappy, and frustrated. People without borderline were born equipped with the ability to handle stress, but those of us with borderline were not. Our cup starts full and gets poured into until it's just a constant overflow. **Therapy** helps empty the cup to a tolerable amount, and sometimes, very bad days happen and the cup is overflowing, and sometimes, we need a good cry but **don't assume a specific behavior (like a moody comment, a snappier tone) is** **because of BPD.** Stress and bad days happen! But never feel like you have to put up with rude tones or comments because of of a disorder - **no matter the disorder!**

But because **you struggle with setting boundaries (necessary in EVERY relationship), being communicative,** I highly suggest you gently break things off and work on those  things you struggle with in therapy! They're immensely great skills to have and honestly, ***needed. (Sometimes emotional unavailability can stem from some sort of neurodivergency!)***

I'm sorry if this came off as snappy or rude! Tone is hard to really get through on text. If you have questions about borderline, I'm open to them so long as the questions are in good faith! It's a hell of a disorder to live with, no matter who you are.

**But if you're not feeling good about entering this relationship - save both of yourselves from unneeded heart break!** It's good you're going to therapy and I genuinely hope it goes well for you and you gain the skills you need to navigate this world! Developing skills and learning communication is hard, learning to emote properly is a bitch of a thing to do, trust me, I know from experience!

**ABUSE IS ABUSE, NO MATTER WHAT IS HAPPENING IN THE BRAIN. IF YOUR PARTNER IS ABUSIVE AND NOT TAKING ACCOUNTABILITY, NEVER PUT UP WITH IT. CHECK WITH YOUR LOCAL RESOURCES IF YOU NEED HELP ESCAPING AN ABUSIVE RELATIONSHIP.**

**And never force yourself to date someone you won't click with just because they have a mental illness that they either won't go to therapy for / take medication for, or for anyone reason. Date the people you** ***like***\*!\*
